A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their main text, equations, results and appendices support reliable comparison. An overlap on v3 page 18 obscures part of Figure 8 visually, but its underlying text remains extractable.

before.justification: v1 reports original probe-training experiments, comparisons with LLM monitors, cascade evaluations, ablations and appendix analyses of calibration and stakes labels.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds smaller-model probe experiments, chain-of-thought baseline evaluations and quantitative distribution-shift analyses.

M1.justification: The six probe architectures, training approach and cascade procedure using median-ranked selection and averaged scores are retained. v1 Table 1 becomes v3 Table 3 in Appendix A.1. Testing attention probes on smaller models does not introduce a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training coverage and six principal evaluation datasets, listed in v1 Table 3 and v3 Table 2. The manual red-teaming and deception/MASK analyses are also retained. The additional experiments reuse existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.8 and Table 8 add chain-of-thought variants for the six Llama/Gemma prompted baselines, plus DeepSeek V3 0324 and Claude Sonnet 4.0. This substantially expands the evaluated monitoring comparators beyond the retained direct-prompting, finetuning and word-statistics baselines.

E3.justification: Additional appendix evaluations introduce 8B and 27B probe backbones with layer selection over every fifth layer, scratchpad generation for CoT baselines, and token-length, token-distribution KL and perplexity measurements. The original data splits, training hyperparameters and AUROC/TPR evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of dependence on the monitored model's size in B.7, quantitative analysis of distribution shift in C.7, and dataset-specific error examples in C.8. These substantially extend robustness and failure analysis beyond the retained architecture, sample-efficiency, calibration and cascade analyses.

E5.justification: The three-run evaluations, five-run deployment-adaptation experiments, confidence intervals and annotation-agreement uncertainty reporting are retained. The new model comparisons do not introduce additional run-count or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Table 12's token-length standard deviations describe dataset dispersion.

E6.justification: New results include mean AUROCs of 0.887 and 0.913 for the smaller-model probes, CoT results such as 0.959 for Gemma-3-12B and 0.960 for Claude Sonnet 4.0, and Table 12's distribution statistics. Original plotted results are largely retained. However, B.7's prompted Llama-3.3-70B value of 0.929 conflicts with Table 8's 0.970 and Figure 3.

T1.justification: The probe functional forms, cascade scoring formula and computational-cost derivations are unchanged. Describing theta as a vector or set of vectors clarifies the existing attention-probe definition. The new distribution metrics do not introduce a theoretical result or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v3 elevates adaptation with as few as 32 deployment samples into a fourth stated contribution. Its abstract and conclusion explicitly condition computational savings on reusing available activations, an assumption already documented in v1 Appendix A.3. The central detection, generalization and cascade claims remain stable.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets smaller-model results as supporting deployment flexibility and attributes CoT disadvantages to latency and instruction-following failures. Appendix C.8 adds explanations involving missing context, noisy language and domain-specific stakes. The original limitations concerning labeling, generalization and adversarial vulnerability remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 supplies exact instruction-tuned model identifiers and repository references. The code/data access pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository. Additional analyses specify layer-search and metric-computation details; the existing hardware and training disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds and discusses Cunningham et al. (2025), Hua et al. (2025) and Oldfield et al. (2025), relating the work to representation reuse, budget-constrained monitoring and polynomial classifiers. These update the research positioning while retaining its principal novelty claims and earlier literature.

P1.justification: Related work is condensed and rewritten, model terminology is standardized, and the separate conclusion and future-work sections become a combined closing section. Detailed future work moves to Appendix D, and probe formulas move to A.1. Most of the original methodological and experimental narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 7, 8 and 12, relocates the probe-definition table, adjusts Figure 4's axis labels and reflows existing figures. Most graphics are retained. A layout regression on page 18 places Figure 9 over the bottom of Figure 8, obscuring some hyperparameters and its caption.

improvement.justification: The smaller-model and CoT comparisons, quantitative distribution-shift analysis and explicit model identifiers improve empirical support and reproducibility while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited by inconsistent baseline values in B.7 versus Table 8/Figure 3, sparse CoT protocol details, and the page-18 overlap obscuring hyperparameters. These defects temper the benefits without undermining the retained central results.
